title: Playing the West End with Frank Williams and Phil Schaap's venue
summary: Durham returned to New York about four years ago, played the West End with Frank Williams, then discusses a feud and the struggling Third Phase.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, when you sort of returned to the picture, it was in New York, when you--
Four years ago.
When you started playing in the West End.
Yeah, four years ago. I stayed at the West End two and a half years and I've been out of there now about four months.
Now at the West End, you usually played with whom?
I played all the time there with Frank Williams.
Right.
Yeah.
But did you know him well before that or not?

No, I didn't know him until -- he got acquainted with me through my cousin Hank Durham in Toledo, Ohio, who was a promoter. Hank Durham, used to (inaudible) played me. So, he give my number to Frank and told Frank to
come and see me and Frank come over and that's how I got in with Frank, because I didn't want to be a leader. But I can go back in the West End anytime I want (inaudible) band (inaudible).
Yeah.
(Inaudible) in touch with him. But I didn't go in there because I had trouble with Phil Shepp. There seemed to be a feud between them and the musicians are sticking with Phil.
Yes, that's sticking with Phil against the management?
Yeah, and they ain't working though noplace.
But didn't he open that new place, The Third Phase? Didn't he?

It ain't doing much. I was over there one Friday and I was over there one Monday and Tuesday. So, he's been trying to run them Mondays and Tuesdays and Wednesdays, like that, and he ain't doing well and he's losing money. He came in one Tuesday (inaudible) told him he should close it all up because I didn't want to come back (inaudible) too short of money, you know?
Well, they don't have any liquor license, do they?
No, everybody's bring their own drink
in there.
: (Inaudible).
(Inaudible) bring you own, bring your package.
: Well, do they charge?
A couple of dollars on the door.
: Oh, I see.
(Inaudible) make it that way. Otherwise, I don't know what they charge. If the (inaudible) --
: Oh well, they can't --
They selling food (inaudible). He's trying to run a door-charge dance and that's all it is.
: Well, didn't he start a place down in mid-town, but that seemed to run one week or something?
I don't know what happened there, because he sent for me, they ask me to come up there (inaudible).
